title: From Guesswork to Experimentation: A Product Teardown of YouTube’s New Video A/B Testing Feature
excerpt: Product teardown of new A/B testing feature of youtube
contentHtml:
A product teardown of YouTube’s new Video A/B Testing feature

Until now, YouTube creators have had to answer a difficult question before publishing a video:

“What version of this video will keep people watching?”

The answer has traditionally come from experience, intuition, analytics, and increasingly, AI.

But intuition has a fundamental limitation.

A creator can believe one opening hook is better than another. another can believe a shorter introduction will improve retention. You can believe a different storytelling structure will keep viewers engaged.

But until real viewers watch it, you don’t really know.

YouTube’s latest Video A/B Testing feature changes that.

Announced at Made on YouTube 2026, YouTube is extending its existing experimentation capabilities from titles and thumbnails to the actual video itself. Creators will be able to test up to three different cuts of a video and determine which version holds audience attention best.

At first glance, this looks like another creator analytics feature.

I think it is something much bigger:

YouTube is turning experimentation into a native part of the content creation workflow. To increase viewers retention.

Consumer: The Creator

To understand the feature as a product, the first question is:

Who is the customer?

For Youtube, The obvious answer is the viewer.

But for this particular product, the primary customer is the creator.

A YouTube creator isn’t simply uploading a video.

They are making dozens of decisions:

  • What topic should I cover?

↓

  • How should I structure it?

↓

  • What should the opening hook be?

↓

  • How long should the introduction be?

↓

  • Which sections should I cut?

↓

  • Where should I reveal the key information?

↓

  • What title should I use?

↓

  • Which thumbnail should I choose?

Historically, many of these decisions have been made before publishing.

The creator makes a version, publishes it, and then watches the analytics.

That creates a fundamental product problem, which is :

The cost of learning is high.

If a creator discovers that their first 30 seconds are weak, they have already published the video.

If they discover that a different opening would have performed better, they cannot go back and expose the same audience to the alternative version in a controlled experiment.

They can edit and re-upload.

But that introduces a completely different set of variables.

  • The audience is different.
  • The timing is different.
  • The recommendation system is different.
  • The initial momentum is different.

So the creator is left asking:

Did this version actually perform better, or did something else change?

YouTube’s Existing Experimentation Strategy

This isn’t YouTube’s first attempt to solve this problem.

YouTube already introduced A/B testing for thumbnails and later expanded it to titles and thumbnails.

That feature allows creators to test up to three variants and has already been used for more than 40 million experiments since its launch in 2024.

The evolution of this feature is :

Phase 1

Thumbnail

Which thumbnail (visual) gets viewers interested?

Thumbnail a/b testing and how it looks

Phase 2

Title + thumbnail

Which title and thumbnail (package) gets the right viewers to click?

Title a/b testing and how it looks

Phase 3

Video itself

Which version of the same video actually keeps them watching?

Video a/b testing

  • YouTube is essentially moving the experimentation layer deeper into the product.

Explaining the New Product — with an example

The new Video A/B Testing feature allows creators to take multiple cuts of the same underlying video and test them against real audiences(viewer side).

For example, imagine a creator makes a video:

“I Tried Building a Startup in 30 Days.”

They could potentially create three openings:

Version A — Story First

“Thirty days ago, I had an idea. Today, I’m going to show you exactly what happened.”

Version B — Result First

“This startup made ₹1.2 lakh in its first month. Here’s how.”

Version C — Conflict First

“By day 12, I was ready to quit.”

The rest of the video could be largely identical. Instead of guessing which hook works best, the creator can just test them out. YouTube can then determine which cut does a better job of holding audience attention.

That changes the creator workflow from: Create → Publish → Analyze to:

Create → Hypothesize → Test → Learn → Publish/Optimize

That is a significant product shift.

The Problem YouTube Is Actually Solving

The problem statement would be:

“Creators don’t know which video version performs best.”

But I think the deeper problem is:

Creators have very limited ability to validate creative decisions before committing to them.

This matters because video creation is inherently uncertain.

IDK who she is — just googled confused creator image for a better reading experience for you

A creator doesn’t know beforehand:

  • which hook will work
  • how quickly they should get to the point
  • whether viewers will tolerate a long introduction
  • whether a different narrative structure will improve retention
  • which moments are causing viewers to leave

Analytics tell you what happened.

They don’t necessarily tell you: What should I have done instead? A/B testing closes that gap.

From Analytics to Experimentation

This is where I think YouTube’s product strategy becomes particularly interesting. Traditional YouTube Studio analytics are largely diagnostic.

You look at a retention graph and discover:

A lot of people left at 42 seconds.

That’s useful

But it still leaves the creator asking:

Video A/B testing moves Studio toward being prescriptive and experimental. Instead of only saying: “People are leaving here.” YouTube can help creators answer: “Does Version B solve the problem?”

That is a fundamentally different product capability.

The Metric Choice Matters

YouTube’s historical approach to experimentation provides an important clue about how it thinks about this problem.

For thumbnail testing, YouTube deliberately moved away from optimizing purely for CTR(Clickthrough rate) and instead uses watch-time-based outcomes because a thumbnail can generate clicks without delivering on the promise of the video.

The same philosophy makes sense for video experimentation. Imagine:

Cut A

Higher initial click-through, But viewers leave quickly.

Cut B

Slightly slower start, But viewers remain engaged for much longer.

If YouTube optimized only for an early engagement signal, Cut A might win. But if the goal is to create videos that actually satisfy viewers, attention retained over the experience is a much better north-star direction. This aligns with YouTube’s own explanation of Studio analytics: watch time matters because it reflects not just getting someone to click, but delivering on the promise and creating returning viewers.

The Creator Value Proposition

For creators, the value proposition is straightforward:

“I think this version will perform better.”

“Let’s test it.”

That sounds simple. But it fundamentally changes creator behavior. A creator who can cheaply experiment is more likely to test:

  • different hooks
  • different pacing
  • different storytelling structures
  • different visual sequences
  • different openings
  • potentially different lengths

Instead of relying entirely on intuition, creators can build an evidence base around what works for their audience. The feature therefore doesn’t just optimize individual videos. It can potentially make creators better at creating videos over time.

What Does YouTube Get?

This is where the product becomes particularly interesting from a PM perspective. YouTube isn’t building this purely for creator goodwill. There is a clear platform-level value exchange.

If creators understand what makes their audiences watch, they can produce better content. Better creators are more likely to:

  • grow their channels
  • publish more consistently
  • monetize successfully
  • build larger audiences
  • stay on YouTube

So YouTube has an incentive to improve the creator’s ability to create more engaging content.

If creators systematically test their videos, more successful versions are likely to emerge. That means the platform potentially gets:

Better hooks → Better retention → Better videos

The quality of YouTube’s content ecosystem can improve without YouTube having to manually decide what every creator should make. It is effectively giving creators the tools to optimize their own content. And more retention means more ad. revenue generated per viewer.

This is the most important downstream effect.

YouTube’s business depends on viewers finding content they want to watch. If experiments help creators remove weak openings, improve pacing, and tell better stories, viewers may get to valuable content faster and remain engaged longer. That can contribute to:

Better viewer experience → More meaningful viewing → Stronger platform engagement

The creator wins.

The viewer wins.

YouTube wins.

There is another, less obvious benefit. Every experiment produces information. Suppose thousands of creators test:

  • 10-second hooks vs. 30-second hooks
  • story-first vs. result-first openings
  • different pacing
  • different structures

YouTube gets an enormous amount of behavioral data about what different audiences respond to. That creates a potential feedback loop:

Creators experiment

↓

YouTube observes

↓

YouTube learns

↓

Creators receive better recommendations/tools

↓

Creators experiment again

The experimentation system can therefore become a learning engine for the entire platform.

The Bigger Strategic Move: YouTube Studio as a Creative Partner

This feature makes even more sense when viewed alongside YouTube’s other 2026 Studio announcements.

YouTube is adding tools for:

  • analyzing past performance
  • discovering content opportunities
  • getting feedback on drafts
  • generating channel-matched thumbnails
  • dynamic thumbnails
  • conversational editing
  • video A/B testing

YouTube explicitly describes Studio as evolving into an end-to-end creative partner across production, packaging, and channel strategy. That’s the bigger product strategy.

YouTube isn’t simply building analytics.It is trying to own more of the creator’s workflow.

And drumroll, My guess is they will monetise this feature as somewhat premium behind a paywall later considering the number of youtube creators are exploding day — by — day.

The creator journey becomes:

Idea

↓

Research

↓

Draft

↓

Edit

↓

Package

↓

Experiment

↓

Publish

↓

Analyze

↓

Learn

↓

Create again

And YouTube increasingly has a product at every step.

The Flywheel

This creates an interesting platform flywheel:

Better creator tools

↓

Lower cost of experimentation

↓

More creator experimentation

↓

Better content

↓

Higher viewer satisfaction

↓

More creator success

↓

More creators invest in YouTube

↓

More content + more experimentation data

↓

Better YouTube

The key insight is that creator success is not separate from YouTube’s success. It is an input into it.

Why This Is a Smart Product Decision

From a PM perspective, I see three particularly strong decisions here.

1. Reduce the cost of experimentation

Creators don’t have to choose between competing creative hypotheses blindly. YouTube provides the infrastructure.

2. Move experimentation closer to creation

Historically, analytics happened after publishing.

YouTube is increasingly bringing measurement and experimentation into the creation workflow itself. That is a major product evolution.

The Product Questions that i think is still there

The feature is promising, but it also raises interesting product questions.

Will small creators have enough traffic?

A/B testing needs enough viewers to produce a meaningful signal. A large creator might reach statistical confidence quickly. A creator with 500 views may struggle.

This creates a potential divide between creators who can experiment frequently and those who cannot.

How different should the cuts be?

If Version A and Version B differ by only two seconds, detecting a meaningful difference may be difficult. But if the versions are dramatically different, the experiment may no longer isolate a single variable.

This creates an interesting UX challenge:

How much experimentation guidance should YouTube provide?

Could creators optimize for retention at the expense of storytelling?

Any metric creates incentives.

If creators learn that certain hooks maximize retention, they could increasingly optimize toward those patterns. The long-term product challenge is therefore making sure:

Optimization ≠ homogenization.

YouTube has to help creators learn without making every video feel engineered by the same playbook.

We all used to watch that one creator that we got bored of that created the same type of videos.

My PM Take

The most interesting part of YouTube’s Video A/B Testing isn’t that creators can test three videos. It’s that YouTube is changing the unit of optimization.

Previously:

Optimize the packaging, Now: Optimize the experience itself.

YouTube is effectively saying:

Don’t guess what viewers will like. Create multiple hypotheses, put them in front of viewers, learn from the result, and use that learning to become a better creator.

Creators provide the content. Viewers provide the behavioral signal. YouTube provides the experimentation infrastructure.

Everyone contributes something, and everyone potentially benefits.

Final Product Lesson

The lesson I take from this feature as a product manager is simple:

Great platforms don’t just give users analytics. They give users mechanisms to act on what the analytics are telling them.

YouTube already had retention graphs. Now it is giving creators a way to experiment against those retention problems.

That is the difference between: “Here’s what happened.”

and “Let’s find out what works.”

And that shift — from analytics to experimentation — is what makes YouTube’s Video A/B Testing more interesting than just another creator feature.

— Will be back with another product breakdowns,

Himanshu Giri

title: How Jiohotstar shows you and 80 million Indians IPL live, in your mobile phone in almost real time, Networking for Beginner.
contentHtml:
Topics discussed below :

  • Networking technique
  • Content delivery networks (CDNs)
  • Adaptive bitrate technology (ABR), IN THIS ORDER.

Before IPL, what is a network? Network is a system or group of devices that are interconnected and can share data with each other.

There are 5 major components in a network, what are they?

1) Sender — In our case the sender is the system that is sending the video that the cameras are capturing at the stadium after processing it into a transmission suitable format (encoding). Generally these systems are in the stadium premises.

2) Receiver — your made in china phone on which you are watching the match livestream(That finally receives data).

3) Transmission medium — As data cannot be transported by pigeons in modern times sadly, there is need of something called transmission medium which acts as physical pathway through which data is being transmitted from sender to receiver. In our case from the stadium’s cameras to your mobile phone. Transmission medium can be wired such as optical fiber cable or wireless technologies such as Wi-Fi, 4g or 5g networks using radio waves. Choice depends on what is more technically feasible example : from stadium to server high-speed optical fiber is used, for last mile delivery to mobile devices 4g/5g is used.

4) Data — The information that the receiver gets from the sender, In our case the video footage from the various stadium cameras.

5) Protocols — The rules followed for data transmission for successful communication between sender to receiver.

Now that we know the major relevant components for networking though there are many more but this much is enough to understand the topic. We should discuss how it really works for that I am going to use step by step explanation approach making it easy to understand :-

STEP 1-

(A)To see the match in video which is different from the live scores on cricbuzz, we need HD cameras that can take up the video of the match, not only 1 but many because if we have a camera that is taking up the video of the leg side and the player plays a shot over covers we need to capture that and show it too.

Now that we have cameras focused on every angle, we need to get all the footages to a system so that from there we can control the footage that is needed to be shown on stream at any particular time and that changes ball by ball.

(B) Now we get the final footage: various angles, crowd reaction footages, advertisements, etc. This final video footage is first encoded and compressed using video codecs such as H.264, converting the video into a binary format (0s and 1s). This encoding process reduces the file size and prepares the video for efficient streaming.

Once encoded, the video data is further broken into data packets and processed according to the four networking layers conceptually present in every device that can be networked: Network access, Internet, Transport, Application layer(TCP/IP model). Finally, the binary data is converted into electrical signals for wired transmission or light signals for fiber optic transmission. At this stage, our video footage is now in the form of an electrical or optical signal, ready to be transmitted.”

So all in all in this step our video footage is now in the form of a signal that is electrical or optic signal.

STEP 2-

  1. The signal is transmitted from the stadium’s system to the jiocinema’s central servers which can be located in Mumbai through high-speed optical fiber cable and the speed of transmission can reach 200,000,000 meters per seconds(2 lakh km/sec)!! in ideal case scenario which is about 2/3rd of the speed of light in vacuum.
  1. And we as viewers are connected to the jiocinema’s CDNs(edge servers, placed near us) and requesting data which is the video footage of the match, and the stadium’s system is providing the video footage of the match in the form of signals.

STEP 3-

  1. Now jiocinema will process the data according to its designed system and will route it through its wide range of content delivery networks(CDNs) which are network of servers placed at different parts of the country depending on some factors such as population density, users demand and more. For example, in a densely populated area like Delhi, CDN edge servers will be more strategically placed compared to a region like Manipur, which has lower demand. CDNs are critical in order to balance load across servers and reducing the response time(latency). Now, for mobile users the CDN will transmit the data to the local mobile towers in which your phone is connected to, through cell networks.

STEP 4- FINAL STEP.

  1. Now the local mobile tower will transmit the data to your mobile phone. And now finally we can see the match. Right? But the data our phone received is still encoded in the binary form like 0s and 1s.
  1. Therefore in the last and final step the received binary data which we need in video format is decoded back using video decoding algorithms such as h.264 and gets reassembled back frame by frame like it was disassembled making a video live stream.

ALL HAIL CSK

Content Delivery Networks: Used for reducing latency and balancing load.

Analogy -CDNs work like food delivery — keeping popular dishes ready at nearby restaurants(similar to caching).

Suppose dominos attempts delivery from one outlet across Delhi, it will put load on that single outlet(Origin server), increasing fulfilment time(latency) and reducing quality but what if there are many branches of dominos(CDNs) opened in different parts of the city it will :

a) Reduce the load(from origin server)

b) Reduce latency, and

c) Improving overall user experience.

Just like that, CDNs cache and serve content from locations closer to the user, instead of always relying on the original server far away.

ABR: JioCinema uses this technology to stream live content even on slow internet connections.

adaptive bitrate streaming: ABR is a technology used to deliver the best video quality based on the internet speed and available network bandwidth on the current network. according to the congestion.

ABR works by encoding the livestream in various different quality levels like 240p, 360p, 480p, 720p, 1080p, 1440p, 2160p i.e. 4k(bitrate ladders). The Jiocinema’s player repeatedly checks the network bandwidth(maximum data transfer capacity) as well as GPU, CPU capacity based on this the player plays the best stream quality that the particular device and its network bandwidth can handle. This process is dynamic, meaning this whole process repeats itself after small time intervals(few seconds) since available network bandwidth also changes with change in the network congestion.

  • Now all this technology takes a lot of money and good engineers to be implemented smoothly for 63 million(current peak) concurrent live viewers, and jiocinema streams IPL for free, but it is also a FOR PROFIT organisation so how do they make money?

→ Through ADS.

JioCinema employs different ad tech solutions that optimize ad selection, timing, and duration to enhance user engagement and correct targeting of ads to people, which is fascinating in itself. More on that in the next article. TEST PORT

title: Massive Ordnance Penetrators(MOPs) GBU57 dropped by b2 bomber in Iran
contentHtml:
Today the US dropped bombs on the nuclear enrichment facility of Iran, what bombs were they? and how they work?

Written out of my love for great weapon systems — Himanshu

Topics mentioned:

  1. about nuclear weapon
  1. Uranium enrichment using gas centrifuges
  1. Massive ordnance penetrators (MOPs)
  1. B2- spirit stealth bomber.

clarity on nuclear weapon :

  • For making a nuclear weapon- Uranium or plutonium is used, now in Iran’s case they are using uranium for the weapon.
  • now most of the naturally occuring uranium is U238 which does not support chain reaction(the base for a nuclear bomb), for that U235 isotope is used which supports it, but the naturally occuring uranium is U238 having just 0.7% of U235, now this is the reason why something called “enrichment” is required to get more of the U235 isotope,
  • Enrichment is basically done to increase the amount of U235 isotope which supports chain reaction on which a nuclear weapon is based.

ENCRICHMENT STAGES

naturally occuring uranium (0.7% U-235)

↓

nuclear power plant grade, electricity gen.(20% U-235)

↓

nuclear weapon grade (> = 90% U-235)

  • Iran’s uranium enrichment levels have reached 60% according to US/Israel intelligence sources

. Although nukes can be made with slightly less than 90% enriched uranium, but it will not be as efficient/damaging.

For this enrichment process Iran uses — gas centrifuges :

  • To spin UF6(uranium hexafluoride) gas at high speed to separate lighter U-235 from heavier U-238.
  • Now these gas centrifuges are hidden inside 80–90 metres inside earth which can only be destroyed by either a small scale nuclear weapon, or massive ordnance penetrator bombs. Normal missiles cannot reach those depths.

gas centrifuges for enriching uranium, inside bunkers

uranium enriching gas centrifuge, hidden inside bunker

now, what is MOPs :

MOPs are “massive bunker buster bombs”, which serves the purpose of destroying deep hidden targets, buried in either bunkers or concrete deep inside earths surface. which most missiles cannot do.

specifications :

height — 20feet(key design aspect) ; weight : 13.6 tons(key design aspect) ; explosive warhead : 2.5 tons. ; most of the bomb is just highly dense steel(80–90%) which gives it its critical weight, and then around 10–20% of the rest is warhead.

working :

  • MOPs are relied on gravity and does NOT have any active propulsion, thus it needs to be dropped from a great height, using its massive weight & height to generate a lot of kinetic energy to penetrate hard inside concrete and rock surfaces, and after the bomb enters its maximum depth through the KE generated by its weight, it uses delayed detonation of warhead to generate maximum destruction thus levelling the whole bunker area.
  • USA used the GBU57 bomb for this job which is a MOP bomb.
  • upon dropping, the bomb cannot change its trajectory like a guided missile. they can only do some minor adjustments with its fins.

WHY MOPs :

  • Conventional weapons cannot penetrate that deep inside a hardened surface, while a mop can take down a 200feet deep target.

WHY USE THE B2-SPIRIT BOMBER

  • well simply because the missile weight 13 tons, and this amount of payload can only be carried by a special bomber internally, and currently the b-2 spirit stealth bomber is the only certified aircraft that can drop this much payload. and also its stealth capability makes it the perfect aircraft to level the bunker.
  • While the enemy’s radar will think of it as a bird the bird will drop a 13 ton bomb and leave.
  • another reason is B2s massive range.

some points :

  • These bombs serve another purpose apart from its main use of destruction, which is power projection.
  • showing technological superiority over the enemy is another aspect, to reduce any chances of retaliation.
  • In other terms — “भय बिनु होई न प्रीति”
